title: ZAM
focus_question: How does ZAM keep people capable while AI takes on more of their work?

statements.label: ZAM
statements.text: ZAM turns everyday work with an AI agent into active-recall practice, so automation sharpens skills instead of eroding them.

statements.label: Beliefs
statements.text: ZAM rests on six beliefs: theses, not proven truths, that evidence may overturn.

statements.label: Symbiosis
statements.text: Human and AI amplify each other, and their collaboration should evolve as the human's competence grows.

statements.label: Collaboration modes
statements.text: Per concept, collaboration moves from shadowing to copilot to autonomy as retention and stability grow.

statements.label: Practice tasks
statements.text: Even in autonomy, the human gets periodic real practice tasks, not quizzes.

statements.label: Disconnection
statements.text: Delegating without understanding is a safety risk: people cannot act when the agent fails.

statements.label: Quiet observation
statements.text: The best learning happens when the learner barely notices it, so the agent observes instead of interrupting.

statements.label: Two-way learning
statements.text: Agent skills decay too, so the same scheduling applies to what the agent knows.

statements.label: Joint capability
statements.text: The goal is never to make the human unnecessary, but to make human and AI more capable together.

statements.label: Forgetting
statements.text: Forgetting is a signal that reveals weak foundations, and the system responds to it structurally.

statements.label: Again
statements.text: A rating of Again tells the system where to focus; it does not mean the learner failed.

statements.label: Skill decay
statements.text: Automation without practice causes capability loss, in humans and agents alike.

statements.label: Shared knowledge
statements.text: Knowledge is a shared graph of concepts; learning is each person's own journey through it.

statements.label: Token and card
statements.text: A concept and a person's relationship to it are different things and are stored apart.

statements.label: Prerequisite graph
statements.text: Concepts build on each other in directed, acyclic prerequisite relations that are the same for every learner.

statements.label: Learning in work
statements.text: Learning works best inside real, meaningful work; isolated flashcards are the fallback.

statements.label: Work session
statements.text: A work session, not a flashcard deck, is the natural container for learning.

statements.label: Work context
statements.text: Learning something while deploying production leaves a stronger trace than flashcard number 47.

statements.label: Mixed topics
statements.text: Mixing topics during review trains telling concepts apart, not just recognising them.

statements.label: Open kernel
statements.text: The learning kernel must not depend on any AI vendor, programming language or interface.

statements.label: Stable contract
statements.text: Published protocol fields are a covenant: new ones may be added, existing ones are never removed or retyped.

statements.label: Funded learning
statements.text: Learning is free to the learner when those who benefit from an informed person fund it.

statements.label: Connector
statements.text: ZAM connects funders and learners but never holds money, which keeps its fee at or below 1%.

statements.label: Named funder
statements.text: Funded content always names who paid for it.

statements.label: Kernel
statements.text: An AI-agnostic kernel holds all learning logic and never calls a language model.

statements.label: Model calls
statements.text: The kernel has zero LLM dependencies; anything that needs HTTP is injected from outside.

statements.label: CLI
statements.text: The CLI is thin orchestration: open the database, call the kernel, render the result, close.

statements.label: CLI models
statements.text: Every model and embedding call lives in the CLI layer, under src/cli/llm.

statements.label: Language models
statements.text: Cloud or local language models evaluate answers and draft content once the learner connects one.

statements.label: Same schedule
statements.text: Scheduling is pure: the same card, rating and time give the same result on every surface.

statements.label: Local library
statements.text: By default, all data lives in one local SQLite database, shared by the agent and the Studio.

statements.label: Server library
statements.text: A library can instead live on Turso or PostgreSQL, behind the same database contract.

statements.label: Machine config
statements.text: Machine-specific state lives in ~/.zam/config.json, never in the shared database.

statements.label: Knowledge model
statements.text: Knowledge is stored as shared concepts; each learner's progress is a personal card on top of them.

statements.label: Token
statements.text: A token is a shared practice item: its wording, Bloom level, domain and an optional source link.

statements.label: Card
statements.text: A card is one learner's FSRS state for one token: stability, difficulty, due date and lapses.

statements.label: Personal queue
statements.text: A concept enters a learner's queue only once that learner has a card for it.

statements.label: Learn first
statements.text: Prerequisite edges mean "learn this first" and connect tokens, never cards.

statements.label: Bloom level
statements.text: A token's Bloom level, from 1 to 5, shapes how its recall question is asked.

statements.label: Five objects
statements.text: The central model separates learning atoms, alignments, curriculum bindings, practice items and cards.

statements.label: Review
statements.text: Reviews use active recall, scheduled by FSRS-6 spaced repetition over a prerequisite graph.

statements.label: FSRS-6
statements.text: FSRS-6 schedules every card with 21 trained weights and a 90% retention target.

statements.label: SM-2
statements.text: SM-2 is the classic spaced-repetition algorithm behind early SuperMemo and Anki.

statements.label: Recall grades
statements.text: Again means recall failed; Hard, Good and Easy all mean it succeeded, with different effort.

statements.label: Blocking
statements.text: Rating Again on a token with prerequisites blocks its card until those foundations have been reviewed.

statements.label: Direct prerequisites
statements.text: Only direct prerequisites surface, never the whole ancestor chain, so one lapse cannot start an avalanche.

statements.label: Unblocking
statements.text: A blocked card returns once every direct prerequisite has been reviewed and is itself unblocked.

statements.label: Mixed queue
statements.text: The review queue mixes domains and slots a new card into every fifth position.

statements.label: Answer format
statements.text: Every rating records how it was answered: free recall, tapped options, or a chosen answer.

statements.label: Tap ceiling
statements.text: A tapped answer never books an interval longer than 20 days.

statements.label: Voice review
statements.text: Voice mode reads cards aloud and maps spoken words to ratings, so review works on a walk.

statements.label: Agents
statements.text: Learning happens inside the AI agent people already use, connected to ZAM through MCP.

c4.name: AI agent app
c4.technology: Claude Code, Codex, VS Code and others

statements.label: MCP
statements.text: zam mcp is the preferred agent connection; the JSON bridge CLI is the fallback.

statements.label: Agent connect
statements.text: zam agent connect writes the MCP registration for eleven supported agent apps.

statements.label: JSON bridge
statements.text: Every bridge response is JSON, errors included, and protocol.ts is its stable contract.

statements.label: In-app panels
statements.text: MCP Apps panels show recall, the learning graph, the knowledge base and a repository's knowledge map inside the agent app.

statements.label: Observed steps
statements.text: ZAM watches the work and quietly marks a step learned when the learner does it well unaided.

statements.label: Capture consent
statements.text: Screen capture is off until the learner turns it on for the machine; then the host allows the call and ZAM's policy limits what it sees.

statements.label: Learner
statements.text: A learner works on real tasks with an AI agent and keeps what they learn through ZAM's reviews.

statements.label: Studio and mobile
statements.text: The Desktop Studio and the mobile apps handle setup, learning content and focused review.

statements.label: Desktop Studio
statements.text: The Desktop Studio is a Tauri app for setup, learning content and focused review.

statements.label: Studio setup
statements.text: Setup that learners see belongs in the Studio, never only on the command line.

statements.label: No terminal
statements.text: Many learners never open a terminal.

statements.label: Light first run
statements.text: First run stays light: optional upgrades never block getting started.

statements.label: Mobile app
statements.text: ZAM Mobile runs standalone on Android and iOS, with no desktop, account or network required.

statements.label: Optional pairing
statements.text: Pairing a phone with a server library by QR code is an optional upgrade.

statements.label: Local models
statements.text: Local text and image generation is offered only on an NPU, a discrete GPU or Apple Silicon.

statements.label: Slow CPU
statements.text: On a CPU, generation finishes but is too slow to review with, and slow reviews mean no reviews.

statements.label: Tauri
statements.text: The desktop app and the mobile apps are built on Tauri 2.

statements.label: Notarized macOS
statements.text: On macOS, ZAM ships notarized with a Developer ID.

statements.label: Mac App Store
statements.text: The Mac App Store's sandbox would cut the app off from the database it shares with the CLI.

statements.label: Learning content
statements.text: Learning content comes from the repo's own knowledge base, curricula, open decks and shared libraries.

statements.label: OKF articles
statements.text: The OKF bundle in docs/okf holds living articles about what is true in this repository now.

statements.label: ADRs
statements.text: OKF articles state current truth; the reasons behind decisions stay in the ADRs.

statements.label: Article cards
statements.text: OKF articles can become learning tokens that cite the article and heading they came from.

statements.label: Curriculum cells
statements.text: Where a curriculum cell covers a learner's position, import goes through that cell first.

statements.label: Generic import
statements.text: Where no cell reaches yet, the manifest-driven curriculum import is the fallback.

statements.label: LehrplanPLUS
statements.text: An import wizard reads Bavaria's LehrplanPLUS curricula for school learners.

statements.label: Open Library
statements.text: The Open Library lists reviewed, openly licensed decks that are pinned and checksummed before import.

statements.label: Anki import
statements.text: Anki packages and CSV or TSV files import without any model or network call.

statements.label: Library topics
statements.text: In a team library, newcomers start by taking topics the library already holds as their own cards.
